newsitem.title: FRANCE: World's oldest person dead at 122.
newsitem.headline: World's oldest person dead at 122.

text.p: Frenchwoman Jeanne Calment, officially the world's oldest person, died on Monday, medical sources said. She was 122.
Calment had celebrated her 122nd birthday last February at the retirement home where she died in the Provencal town of Arles.
The medical sources at the retirement home did not mention the cause of death.

The Guinness Book of Records listed Calment as the oldest person who ever lived -- and has a birth certificate, dated February 21, 1875, to prove the claim. It said other rivals for the longevity crown lack documentation.
Calment used to say that a smile and humour were her recipe for long life. "I've only ever had one wrinkle and I'm sitting on it," she once remarked. "I will die laughing," she predicted.
Born into a well-to-do family 10 years after the assassination of U.S. president Abraham Lincoln, she outlived her husband, her daughter who died in 1934 and her grandson, a doctor, who died in 1963.
